slice: rmcp-v3.1.4 Streamable HTTP Parts to RequestContext extension transfer

source_evidence.finding: The Streamable HTTP server receives http::request::Parts and inserts that Parts value into the MCP request's extension map before creating the oneshot transport; the same injection pattern is present in legacy/stateless request branches.
Server dispatch constructs RequestContext with extensions taken from request.extensions_mut(), so the previously inserted http::request::Parts reaches RequestContext.extensions.

result_detail: The previously proposed principal bridge has its critical transport-to-handler link source-qualified at the exact rmcp-v3.1.4 release: inbound HTTP Parts is stored as an MCP request extension, and service dispatch moves MCP request extensions into RequestContext.extensions. Therefore a trusted HTTP middleware principal stored inside Parts.extensions is structurally reachable through RequestContext.extensions.get::<http::request::Parts>() followed by parts.extensions.get::<Principal>(), provided the middleware actually inserts Principal before StreamableHttpService consumes the request. The exact dependency-version Axum/http middleware insertion form was not source-qualified in this bounded slice and remains the next child.
